payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Move the mug so that it is positioned to the right of the headphones.
node.criteria: Apply the original rubric using the supports' grounded evidence, not confidence or pass counts. Return complete when s1 establishes that the requested mug is to the right of the headphones; s2 unknown or skipped must not block this endpoint. Equivalent grounded endpoint evidence in s2 may also establish completion. Otherwise return partial when evidence establishes some requested progress without establishing complete fulfillment, including when endpoint uncertainty coexists with independently established progress. Return absent only when evidence establishes no requested progress; s1 fail alone does not establish absence. Return unknown when neither completion, requested progress, nor absence of progress is established. Unknown and skipped states are not failures. Ambiguous target identity must not be resolved by selecting an arbitrary right-side mug, and unrelated additions or alterations do not count as progress. If support evidence conflicts about target correspondence or placement, preserve uncertainty unless the evidence itself resolves the conflict.
node.binding: Target: The mug is visibly positioned to the right of the headphones.. Reference: The headphones in the image; compare the mug’s position with the headphones..

node_traces.evidence: Neither support establishes where the original mug ended up. The edited image contains multiple mug-like objects, and their correspondence to the source mug is unresolved; therefore neither completion nor requested progress or absence of progress is established.

dependencies.evidence: The source identifies the target as the single light-blue mug with a curved handle left of the black headphones. In the edited image, the headphones are near the center, but there are two distinct mug-like objects: a pale mug immediately to their left and a light-colored mug to their right. The original mug's appearance and correspondence to either edited object cannot be established confidently, especially with the blurred blue area at far left, so its final position is unresolved.

The source has one distinctive light-blue mug left of the headphones. In the edited image, that mug is not clearly identifiable: there is a blue blurred shape at the left and two small white mugs, with no reliable visual correspondence establishing that the source mug was relocated to the headphones’ right. The apparent changes therefore do not establish requested relocation progress.

response.content: {"text":"The binding is too generic to preserve target identity: the source mug is the distinctive light-blue mug with a curved handle, initially left of the headphones. Make the node explicitly compare that source object across the before/after images, rather than treating any mug-like object on the right as the target. But do not let identity ambiguity erase independently visible progress: the edited image shows a mug-like object left of the headphones and another to their right, while the original blue mug appears blurred at far left. The current traces do not establish which edited object is the original, so uncertainty is warranted; the reference label “partial” is an aggregate constraint, not proof that either mug is the target. Improve the node’s criterion to distinguish grounded evidence of partial movement from mere additions or ambiguous correspondence, and preserve unknown when neither is established. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated; the issue is visual identity/evidence ambiguity, not a reason to force a label or lower confidence."}
